facts.statement: Explorornis is a genus of Mesozoic birds named after the Latin word for 'to discover' and the Greek word for 'bird'.
facts.quote: Explorornis ("discovered bird", from Latin explōrō "to discover" and Ancient Greek ornis (όρνις) "bird") is a genus of Mesozoic birds

facts.statement: Explorornis lived around 90 million years ago during the mid-late Turonian stage in the Bissekty Formation of the Kyzyl Kum in present-day Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: which lived during the mid-late Turonian stage, around 90 million years ago, in the Bissekty Formation of the Kyzyl Kum, in present-day Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The two species of Explorornis are named after paleontologists Lev Alexandrovich Nesov and Alick Donald Walker.
facts.quote: The two species are named after famous paleontologists: Lev Alexandrovich Nesov (1947–1995) and Alick Donald Walker.

facts.statement: Most Explorornis species were small birds about 15 to 20 cm long, while E. walkeri was likely over 25 cm long.
facts.quote: These were all smallish birds, maybe 15–20 cm long in life, except E. walkeri which was probably more than 25 cm long.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic position of Explorornis is unresolved because only coracoid fossils are known.
facts.quote: Since only the coracoids are known, the phylogenetic position of these taxa is somewhat unresolved.

facts.statement: Explorornis belongs to the parent group Alexornithidae.
Explorornis is classified within the family Alexornithidae.
Explorornis is classified under the class Reptilia.
Explorornis lived between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
